title: Isandro and the Contact
premise: Tamsin Thackeray, a meticulous financial-crimes investigator, notices that Flight 4472 has vanished from every database while still airborne—a deletion so clean it could only come from inside the agency. Following the ghost flight's money trail, Tamsin uncovers a laundering network run by the very regulators who rewrote the rules they enforce, and finds an unlikely found family in the plane's grounded crew and a whistleblower archivist. When Tamsin's own hidden past becomes the leverage used against them, they must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the people who've become home. In the end, Tamsin leaks everything at the border checkpoint before the night shift changes—burning their career but freeing the crew, the archivist, and themselves.
about_author: Tamsin Yarrow spent a decade auditing shipping manifests in port cities before turning to fiction, and her thrillers are known for procedural precision wrapped around fiercely human hearts. She writes from a rented flat above a defunct travel agency, where she keeps a wall of unsolved flight numbers.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: POV: Tamsin. A routine audit of shell companies reveals nothing—which itself is suspicious, since the money is too clean. Tamsin's colleague jokes that perfection is a confession. The emotional beat is quiet unease: twelve years of rule-following have left Tamsin competent but hollow, going through motions in a life built on procedure instead of people.

chapters.title: Flight 4472
chapters.summary: POV: Tamsin. Cross-referencing customs manifests, Tamsin finds Flight 4472 listed as landed at three airports simultaneously—then gone from all of them while radar logs show it still airborne. Every record erases itself as Tamsin watches. The beat is vertigo: for the first time, the rules don't just fail to protect; they actively lie.

chapters.title: The Crew That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Tamsin and Mara, the flight's purser. Tamsin tracks down the crew, officially 'reassigned,' living in a company dorm with confiscated passports. Mara remembers a sealed cargo container and a passenger who never deplaned. The beat is wary connection—two strangers recognizing each other as disposable to the same machine.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: POV: Tamsin. In a basement records annex, Tamsin meets Dez, a disgraced archivist who hoards deleted data out of spite. Dez confirms the deletion signature belongs to internal oversight software—the watchdogs are eating the evidence. The beat is grim alliance: Tamsin gains an ally and a target on their back in the same breath.

chapters.title: Rules, Rewritten
chapters.summary: POV: Tamsin. New compliance directives arrive overnight, retroactively legalizing the anomalies Tamsin flagged. Their supervisor, Voss, gently suggests a transfer to a quiet posting. The beat is betrayal and clarity: the system isn't broken; it's working exactly as designed, and Tamsin's obedience was always the product being sold.

chapters.title: What Tamsin Buried
chapters.summary: POV: Tamsin, flashback-heavy. Voss reveals he knows about the one secret from Tamsin's past—a falsified report twelve years ago that saved a family but ended a colleague's career. He offers silence in exchange for dropping the investigation. The beat is dread: the loyalty-versus-truth theme turns inward, and Tamsin's clean record was never clean.

chapters.title: The Container
chapters.summary: POV: Mara, then Tamsin. Mara breaks into the impound hangar and photographs the sealed container: bearer bonds and a ledger naming the oversight board members who own the vanished flight. She gets it to Tamsin just as security closes in. The beat is courage and cost—Mara sacrifices her last chance at reinstatement to hand Tamsin the truth.

chapters.title: Found Family, Fractured
chapters.summary: POV: Tamsin. Hiding in Dez's annex with Mara and the ledger, the three form a fragile household of the discarded—shared meals, shared watch shifts, shared fear. Then Voss offers Tamsin a final trade: destroy the ledger and he'll erase the old falsified report forever. The beat is tenderness under siege, making the coming choice unbearable.

chapters.title: Checkpoint
chapters.summary: POV: Tamsin. Tamsin agrees to meet Voss at the border checkpoint where the erased flight's cargo crossed—but plans a double play, seeding the ledger to press outlets timed to the shift change when checkpoint oversight lapses. Voss springs his trap; Dez takes a beating shielding the drive. The beat is the climax: truth and loyalty collide, and Tamsin must let something burn either way.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: POV: Tamsin, closing with Mara. As the night shift changes, the leak goes live: the board falls, the flight's passengers are named, and Tamsin surrenders their badge and their secret together, choosing exposure over protection. Months later, Tamsin, Mara, and Dez share a table in a port-town diner—no longer investigators, just family. The beat is hard-won peace outside the law.
